summary.text: The unlisted number \(n=2^{13}3^6\cdot5\cdot7^6\cdot13^4\cdot17^2=28996592704045424640\) is a fixed point. Multiplicativity on these coprime prime powers, together with the computed component values \(A003958(\sigma(2^{13},3^6,5,7^6,13^4,17^2))=(10584,1092,2,132496,30940,306)\), makes their product equal to \(n\).

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
F(m)=\prod_{p}(p-1)^{v_p(m)},
\]
where the product is over the prime divisors of the positive integer \(m\), and let
\[
a(n)=F(\sigma(n)),
\]
with \(\sigma(n)\) denoting the sum of the positive divisors of \(n\). Thus \(F\) is the sequence A003958 and \(a\) is A351442.

We will exhibit a positive fixed point of \(a\) that is not in the proposed list. Set
\[
N=2^{13}3^6 5\,7^6 13^4 17^2.
\]
In decimal form,
\[
N=28{,}996{,}592{,}704{,}045{,}424{,}640.
\]
In particular, \(N>0\).

We use two elementary multiplicativity facts. First, \(F\) is completely multiplicative on positive integers. Indeed, for every prime \(p\),
\[
v_p(xy)=v_p(x)+v_p(y),
\]
so
\[
F(xy)=\prod_p(p-1)^{v_p(x)+v_p(y)}
     =\left(\prod_p(p-1)^{v_p(x)}\right)
      \left(\prod_p(p-1)^{v_p(y)}\right)
     =F(x)F(y).
\]
Also, if \(q\) is prime, then directly from the definition
\[
F(q)=q-1.
\]
Second, \(\sigma\) is multiplicative on coprime arguments, and for a prime power it satisfies
\[
\sigma(p^e)=1+p+\cdots+p^e.
\]
The six prime powers occurring in \(N\) are pairwise coprime. Therefore
\[
\sigma(N)=
\sigma(2^{13})\sigma(3^6)\sigma(5)\sigma(7^6)
\sigma(13^4)\sigma(17^2).
\]
We now compute these six divisor sums and then apply \(F\) to each one.

For \(2^{13}\), the geometric sum is
\[
\sigma(2^{13})=1+2+\cdots+2^{13}=2^{14}-1=16383.
\]
It factors as
\[
16383=3\cdot 5461=3\cdot43\cdot127.
\]
The numbers \(3,43,127\) are prime. Hence complete multiplicativity of \(F\) gives
\[
F(16383)=(3-1)(43-1)(127-1)
        =2\cdot42\cdot126
        =10584.
\]

For \(3^6\),
\[
\sigma(3^6)=1+3+3^2+\cdots+3^6
=\frac{3^7-1}{3-1}=1093.
\]
The integer \(1093\) is prime, so
\[
F(1093)=1093-1=1092.
\]

For \(5\),
\[
\sigma(5)=1+5=6=2\cdot3.
\]
Thus
\[
F(6)=(2-1)(3-1)=1\cdot2=2.
\]

For \(7^6\),
\[
\sigma(7^6)=1+7+7^2+\cdots+7^6
=\frac{7^7-1}{7-1}=137257.
\]
This factors as
\[
137257=29\cdot4733,
\]
and both \(29\) and \(4733\) are prime. It follows that
\[
F(137257)=(29-1)(4733-1)
=28\cdot4732
=132496.
\]

For \(13^4\),
\[
\sigma(13^4)=1+13+13^2+13^3+13^4=30941.
\]
The integer \(30941\) is prime, and consequently
\[
F(30941)=30941-1=30940.
\]

Finally, for \(17^2\),
\[
\sigma(17^2)=1+17+17^2=307.
\]
The integer \(307\) is prime, so
\[
F(307)=307-1=306.
\]

For completeness, all the primality assertions used above are elementary finite checks. Trial division only by primes at most the square root suffices. For \(43\) these possible divisors are \(2,3,5\), and for \(127\) they are \(2,3,5,7,11\). For \(1093\), one checks the primes through \(31\), since \(\sqrt{1093}<34\). For \(4733\), one checks the primes through \(67\), since \(\sqrt{4733}<69\). For \(30941\), one checks the primes through \(173\), since \(\sqrt{30941}<176\). For \(307\), one checks the primes through \(17\), since \(\sqrt{307}<18\). Division in each case leaves a nonzero remainder. Thus the displayed decompositions are indeed prime factorizations, which is exactly what is required in order to evaluate \(F\).

Applying complete multiplicativity of \(F\) to the displayed factorization of \(\sigma(N)\), we now obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(N)=F(\sigma(N))
&=F(16383)F(1093)F(6)F(137257)F(30941)F(307)\\
&=10584\cdot1092\cdot2\cdot132496\cdot30940\cdot306.
\end{aligned}
\]
To see directly why this product is exactly \(N\), factor its six terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
10584&=2^3 3^3 7^2,\\
1092&=2^2 3\,7\,13,\\
2&=2,\\
132496&=2^4 7^2 13^2,\\
30940&=2^2 5\,7\,13\,17,\\
306&=2\,3^2 17.
\end{aligned}
\]
Collecting the exponents in their product gives
\[
2^{3+2+1+4+2+1}
3^{3+1+2}
5
7^{2+1+2+1}
13^{1+2+1}
17^{1+1}
=2^{13}3^6 5\,7^6 13^4 17^2=N.
\]
Therefore
\[
a(N)=N,
\]
so \(N\) is a positive fixed point of A351442.

On the other hand, the proposed list is
\[
1,\ 2,\ 8,\ 128,\ 288,\ 720,\ 32768,\ 29719872,\ 2147483648.
\]
Every member of this list is at most \(2{,}147{,}483{,}648\), whereas
\[
N=28{,}996{,}592{,}704{,}045{,}424{,}640
>2{,}147{,}483{,}648.
\]
Thus \(N\) is not in the list. It is nevertheless a positive fixed point, so the assertion that the positive fixed points are exactly the nine listed numbers is false.
